qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Legacy relational database and ERP workloads feature formidable switching costs, but lack genuine organic pricing power. Oracle relies on adversarial license audits and predatory maintenance fee hikes (22% annual list price) that alienate enterprise clients and accelerate multi-year migrations to open-source alternatives (PostgreSQL) and hyperscaler platforms (AWS Aurora, Azure SQL). OCI Gen 2 cloud infrastructure is a capital-intensive commodity price-taker competing via compute discounting, while the $28.3B Cerner acquisition continues to bleed EHR market share to Epic Systems.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Moat & Pricing Power, REJECT). Enterprise database switching costs fail the Munger pricing power standard: price increases trigger customer churn and active migration to PostgreSQL, AWS Aurora, and cloud-native alternatives rather than inelastic customer acceptance. OCI cloud infrastructure is an undifferentiated, capital-intensive GPU rental price-taker, and Cerner continues losing share to Epic Systems. Downstream balance sheet is severely overleveraged with >$120B in debt and negative FY2025 FCF.
qualitative.evidence: Historical GAAP ROIC has hovered around 13-14%, but incremental ROIIC is deteriorating sharply as Oracle accelerates capital expenditures ($15B+ in FY2025 vs $6.9B in FY2024) to build speculative AI data centers, driving FY2025 free cash flow negative (-$394M). Database lock-in is defended via punitive License Management Services audits rather than customer surplus, driving Fortune 500 migrations away from Oracle. In cloud IaaS, OCI holds mid-single-digit market share and acts as a price-taker against AWS, Microsoft Azure, and GCP. Healthcare IT subsidiary Cerner ($28.3B purchase in 2022) has suffered VA contract renegotiation pauses and hospital defections to Epic. Furthermore, long-term debt has surged to $122.3B against $12.4B GAAP Net Income (~9.8x Net Debt / NI) with $3.5B+ annual interest expense, which would also catastrophically fail downstream Gate 6.
